items.note: Near-identical to existing bank item nb:nb26-core-057 (older adult with UTI; new confusion, tachypnea, hypothermia as early sepsis cues). Rewritten as a recognize-cues SATA on malignant hyperthermia, a multisystem emergency not otherwise covered in the bank.

Stem now states the nurse is trained in blood culture collection, so the key (draw cultures now, then give the antibiotic) does not depend on an unstated local policy; separates it from bank item nb:nb26-infx-054 (cultures cannot be obtained).

Near-identical to bank item nb:nb-heme-02 (IV antibiotic anaphylaxis; IM epinephrine first); anaphylaxis is also well covered in the heme quizzes. Rewritten as a pharm item on adding IV hydrocortisone for septic shock with an ongoing vasopressor requirement (SSC 2021); key stays at position 3.

Distractor 'Start a dobutamine infusion' was arguably also questionable at a BP of 82/58 mm Hg (current cardiogenic shock guidance favors norepinephrine for hypotension; dobutamine can lower BP). Replaced with norepinephrine titrated to a MAP of 65 mm Hg so the fluid bolus is the only prescription to question.

Same fact as bank items nb:nb-heme-05 and nb:ccrn-heme-03 (DIC laboratory profile). Rewritten as a SATA on recognizing the trauma 'lethal triad' (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy) during massive resuscitation.

Same fact as rnr:heme-009 (bleeding precautions at a platelet count of 32,000/mm³) and nb:u2-rrp-014. Rewritten as a safety SATA on preventing infusion errors when a client in shock has several high-alert continuous infusions.

Same fact as book quiz item resp-ards-q1 (sepsis, bilateral infiltrates, refractory hypoxemia = ARDS); ARDS is covered by 17 quiz items. Rewritten as an analyze-cues item on abdominal compartment syndrome after large-volume resuscitation; key stays at position 2.

Same fact as book quiz items resp-ards-q3 and resp-ards-q12 (low tidal volume by predicted body weight in ARDS). Rewritten as a generate-solutions item on urgent source control (decompression of an obstructed, infected kidney) in septic shock; key stays at position 3.
Reference tjc-npsg did not support rapid response escalation (no current NPSG covers it); replaced with openstax-fund.

Same skill and format as bank item nb:u2-moca-007 (place nurse's statements in SBAR order for a deteriorating postoperative client). Rewritten as an ordered-response prioritization of four clients with shock-related problems.

Same fact as rnr:leadership-040 (SATA on rapid response activation criteria). Rewritten as a SATA on the essential content of a nurse-to-nurse handoff when a client with septic shock transfers to the ICU.
Same fact as bank item nb:nb26-moca-015 (closed-loop communication during a code). Rewritten as a management-of-care item on post-resuscitation team debriefing; key stays at position 0.

Same fact as bank item nb:ccrnb-ethics-25 (family presence during resuscitation with a support person). Rewritten as an item on the primary nurse's role when the rapid response team arrives; key stays at position 1.

Near-identical to bank item nb:nb26-resp-035 and book item heme-anaphylaxis-q6 (glucagon for epinephrine-resistant anaphylaxis in a client on a beta blocker). Rewritten as an analyze-cues pharm item on recognizing dobutamine-induced tachydysrhythmia in cardiogenic shock; key stays at position 1.
Same fact as rnr:immuno-029 (epinephrine auto-injector teaching: outer thigh, through clothing, call EMS, carry two). Rewritten as a pharm SATA on safe norepinephrine titration and monitoring.
